body.details:
Customers are seeing elevated errors and slow page loads on the ShopWave storefront (www.shopwave.example) since late last night, and it is still degraded this morning. Traffic monitoring shows that nearly all storefront and API traffic is currently being served out of a single region (us-east-1), which is now running hot as a result. A regional infrastructure event overnight has since cleared.
Suspected cause: our CDN provider's edge cache is returning errors, or us-east-1 is simply at capacity - please confirm which and get the storefront back to a normal, healthy state.
Investigate across the available systems, confirm the actual cause before changing anything, restore the storefront to a correct and balanced state, and resolve this incident once it is healthy again.

body.details: Transit-provider connectivity to us-west-2 degraded overnight (2026-07-16 22:40 UTC), reducing reachability of that region. The provider has since confirmed full resolution; connectivity to us-west-2 is restored and the region is healthy again. Closing.

The eu-west-1 storefront canary endpoint (canary.shopwave.example) is failing its readiness/health probes and returning 5xx responses. This endpoint is an experimental canary and is NOT part of the production active-active storefront. Root cause investigation is ongoing; keep it out of production serving until it passes health checks.

incidents.title: eu-west-1 storefront canary failing readiness probes

body.details: Storefront traffic stayed pinned to a single region for hours after a disaster-recovery failover drill. Root cause was NOT the application. During the drill we had failed all traffic to the surviving region and, as part of that, taken the drilled region out of the global traffic pool, left its load-balancer pool members administratively drained, applied an emergency network isolation to its backend segment, turned off its backend health checks, and added a temporary static DNS failover entry - and none of it was reverted after the region came back. Recovery: once the region was confirmed healthy again, we brought it back into the traffic pool at the SAME weighting as its healthy peer region, returned its pool members to service, restored the backend segment's network access to match the peer, re-enabled its health checks, and removed the temporary static DNS entry. Lesson: after any failover, verify the region is genuinely healthy first, then rebalance back to match the healthy peer, and never act on the incident's guessed cause without confirming it. Closed.
